profile.entities: Rupa & Company Limited; MUFG Intime (IR / moderator — Omkar Bagwe)
profile.mgmt: Mr. Vikash Agarwal (Whole-time Director); Mr. Sumit Khowala (CFO)
profile.subseg: Economy/mid/premium innerwear; thermals (Thermocot); women's innerwear; athleisure; kidswear; brands Frontline, Macroman, Softline, Euro, Thermocot, Bumchums, Femmora
profile.themes: Athleisure as premiumization / gross-margin lever; geopolitical (US–Iran/Middle East) → crude → raw-material & freight cost; secondary-sales / distribution rebuild theme

bull_bear.body:
- Net cash surplus ₹33 cr (31-Mar-26); OCF FY26 ₹45 cr.
- Short-term debt held deliberately for arbitrage (FD rate > borrowing rate → ~nil net finance cost).
- Dividend ₹3/share proposed for FY26.
- ₹70 cr spent on brand & development in FY26 (mix: outdoor ~50%, TV ~10–12%, print ~12%, digital ~4%; balance ~20% not detailed on call — to be shared separately); future tilt toward digital.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Demand / pricing:** intensely competitive "buyer's market"; pricing pressure persistent across Q3 and Q4; long-run sales CAGR only ~2%.
- **Competition:** hosiery industry "very competitive from the last couple of years" (peers like Page/Jockey, Dollar, Lux, Rupa contested — though competitors not named explicitly on call).
- **Raw material / macro:** US–Iran / Middle East tension → crude up → raw-material cost up; global shipping-route disruption → higher logistics & freight; FX volatility. Yarn shortage.
- **Margin sustainability:** Q4 12.5% EBITDA margin well above 9–10% FY27 guide — Q4 strength may be seasonal/mix-driven, not structural.
- **Execution risk:** entire new sales leadership team is brand-new (appointed in Q4); benefits unproven.
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: - Measured and candid. Acknowledged the difficult, competitive industry and weak long-term CAGR rather than spinning it. Confident on the new sales team and secondary-sales strategy ("the team is in place now... we are sure in coming months we will see the impact"). Cautious/non-committal on yarn pricing ("every day is a new day").
bull_bear.title: Management tone

bull_bear.body:
- The **strong Q4 (12.5% EBITDA) masks a weak FY26** (9.2% EBITDA, both revenue and PAT de-grew) — the headline-friendly quarter contrasts a poor full year.
- **Athleisure is doing the heavy lifting** on margins (vol +20%/val +25%); the broader portfolio remains under pricing pressure.
- Net-debt optics are misleading: short-term debt is an **arbitrage trade**, not a liquidity need (net finance cost ~nil; net cash positive).
- **All key sales hires happened in a single quarter** — a fast, concentrated org rebuild that is the real swing factor for FY27.
- FY27 EBITDA margin guidance (9–10%) is *below* the Q4 print, implying management does not expect Q4 margins to hold for the full year.
- Brand spend stepping UP (4%→6–7%) into FY27 even as margins are guided flat-ish — a deliberate growth investment.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "Sharing profits consistently" — the deck presents an unbroken FY16-FY26 dividend track record, with a special dividend of Rs. 2/- per equity share as a "Mark of gratitude to our shareholders during the pandemic".
- Payout as a % of profits is disclosed for FY16-FY26 with values ranging from 12.5% to 44.9% across the series (see notes — the dividend bar labels could not be reliably bound to years).
- Balance sheet: "Net Cash Surplus stands at Rs. 7 Cr as on Jun'26", which management links to "continued focus on liquidity discipline and financial flexibility".
- Net Working Capital at Jun'26 of Rs. 868 Cr versus Rs. 854 Cr at Mar'26; return ratios are shown for FY22-FY26 (ROCE series 28.4%, 8.5%, 11.9%, 13.7%, 12.2% and ROE series 23.8%, 6.0%, 7.5%, 8.4%, 7.0%).
- Capital deployment is skewed to brand rather than plant: Brand Development Cost is shown at Rs. 78 / 66 / 63 / 69 Cr for FY23-FY26 and Rs. 21 Cr in Q1 FY27; no manufacturing capex programme or spend is disclosed.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Legacy knitwear brand with origins in 1968 and a presence spanning more than five decades in the Indian knitwear market
- Pan-India distribution network comprising over 1,500 dealers and retail reach of more than 2 lakh outlets
- Diversified brand architecture across Economy, Mid-Premium and Premium segments, giving flexibility to respond to changing consumer preferences and varying levels of consumer spending
- Sustained brand investment — advertising and promotional expenditure of H69 crore in FY 2025-26, representing ~5.5% of revenue, across television, print, outdoor and digital media with celebrity endorsements
- Multi-location manufacturing facilities, process standardisation, automation initiatives and quality control systems supporting manufacturing continuity
- Dedicated export unit with traction in the Middle East, South Korea and Italy
- Growing presence across modern trade, e-commerce and quick commerce, which together contributed 5.1% of revenue during the year
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Water availability and effluent compliance in manufacturing — Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications: manufacturing operations depend on adequate water resources, and disruptions from scarcity, changing rainfall patterns and other climate-related factors may disrupt production continuity. Non-compliance with regulations governing water withdrawal, effluent discharge and wastewater management may result in regulatory actions, financial penalties, operational disruptions and reputational risk. Mitigations cited include nano-technology-based water treatment for reuse of processed water, water meters at key withdrawal and consumption points, effluent treatment before discharge and bi-annual quality analysis by NABL-accredited laboratories.
- Chemicals used in dyeing and processing operations — Flagged as a risk with negative financial implications: chemical use exposes the Company to environmental and occupational health and safety risks, and inadequate handling, storage or disposal may affect employee health, surrounding ecosystems and water quality. Evolving regulatory requirements on chemical usage, storage and effluent discharge may increase compliance obligations, with regulatory action on non-compliance. Mitigations cited include advanced treatment technologies to remove dyes and contaminants from process water before discharge, PPE and periodic training for chemical handlers, and Global Organic Textile Standard (GOTS) certification.
- Waste management and circular-economy compliance — Flagged as a risk with negative financial implications: inadequate waste management practices may adversely affect worker health and safety and contribute to contamination of land, water and air, potentially resulting in regulatory non-compliance, financial penalties, reputational damage and increased environmental liabilities. Managed through a compliance-driven approach aligned to State Pollution Control Board regulations, disposal via authorised agencies, 3R principles and sustainable packaging.
- Human rights across operations and the workforce — Listed in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk (item 5, Human Rights), with the Company stating strong emphasis on respecting and protecting human rights and dignity. The bundle is truncated mid-sentence, so the full rationale and mitigation are not readable; regular and structured training programmes to build awareness, competencies and adherence to established safety protocols are described alongside these people-related issues.
- Raw-material price volatility, geopolitical tension and trade-policy change across the apparel value chain — The MD&A industry review states that geopolitical tensions, evolving trade policies, raw material price volatility and supply-chain disruptions remain key challenges for apparel industry participants globally, with implications for cost predictability and margins.
- Energy-cost and inflation headwinds from the West Asia conflict — The MD&A outlook notes that the outbreak of conflict in West Asia since early 2026 has created additional headwinds in the form of higher energy costs, supply chain disruptions and elevated uncertainty, and that the RBI's FY 2026-27 CPI projection of 4.6% remains subject to upside risks from energy-price volatility, geopolitical developments, food-price pressures and potential currency-related imported inflation.
- Competitive intensity and shifting consumer demand in core categories — The Board's report describes performance as resilient 'despite a competitive business environment and evolving consumer demand trends across key product categories'; net profit after tax for FY 2025-26 declined 12.9% year on year even as sales volume grew 4%, showing how exposed earnings are to mix and competitive pressure.
- Concentration in the domestic traditional-trade channel — Structural concentration implied by the disclosed channel split: exports contributed approximately 3% of overall revenue and Modern Trade plus e-commerce 5.1% during the year, leaving the large majority of revenue dependent on the domestic distribution channel and on Indian consumption conditions. Export traction itself is concentrated in the Middle East, South Korea and Italy.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:
- **Athleisure:** Standout — volume +20%, value +25% in Q4; primary driver of GM rebound. "Encouraging momentum," strong consumer acceptance.
- **Mid-premium / premium:** continued focus via product initiatives + calibrated channel expansion (no hard numbers given).
- **Women's / thermal / economy:** not individually quantified on the call.
- **Channel mix (FY26):** Exports ~3% of revenue; Modern trade incl. e-commerce ~5% of revenue. GT (general trade) remains the bulk; mgmt admits "lacking in a lot of GT, a lot of areas in e-commerce."

business.body:

- [Industry TAM] The deck cites a Men's Innerwear Market of 4,300 (2010), 8,500 (2015) and 17,894 (2027E) at 6% CAGR, and a Women's Innerwear Market of 7,000 (2010), 14,500 (2015) and 56,364 (2027E) at 12% CAGR — units are not stated on the slide.
- [Management depth] Named functional heads include a National Sales Head, Head-Exports, Ecommerce Head and GM-Large Format Stores, alongside a Chief Digital & IT Officer — consistent with the channel-expansion agenda.

latest_quarter.body:
- Q4 EBITDA margin 12.5% (+150 bps YoY); gross margin ~28% (rebound from ~26–27%).
- GM improvement **mainly from product mix** (athleisure), plus operating leverage from higher revenue compensating fixed/operational cost.
- **Cotton/yarn:** "shortage of yarn"; pricing normalization over next 1–2 quarters will depend on competition and yarn/cotton prices — "every day is a new day."

- **Trade discount intensity:** ~12% in Q4 (broadly flat vs Q3, still elevated); mgmt expects to "maintain the same level of discount."
- Discounting is dynamic / market-driven (buyer's market).
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost (cotton / yarn)

latest_quarter.body: - **Q4 FY26:** Rev ₹441.5 cr (+6.3% YoY); EBITDA ₹55 cr / 12.5% (+150 bps YoY); PAT ₹36.1 cr / 8.2%. Volume +9%; Athleisure vol +20%/val +25%. GM rebound to ~28%. Net cash ₹33 cr. Dividend ₹3/sh. **FY26 full year:** Rev ₹1,259.1 cr (+1.6%); EBITDA ₹115.3 cr / 9.2% (−11.6%); PAT ₹72.5 cr / 5.8% (−12.9%). Guidance FY27: rev +10–12% (4–5% vol + 4–5% value), EBITDA margin 9–10%, ad-spend 6–7%, capex ₹60 cr over 2 yrs (Kolkata Hosiery Park). outlook.body:
- **FY27 revenue growth: 10–12%**, "largely led by volumes." Split clarified as roughly **4–5% volume + 4–5% value** (mix of both).
- **FY27 EBITDA margin: 9–10%** (note: this is *below* the Q4 12.5% print — guidance is to the full-year level, not the strong Q4).
- **Gross margin:** Mgmt "hopes to sustain" the ~28% Q4 gross margin going forward, supported by initial price hikes and athleisure mix.
- **Profitability trajectory:** targeting ~50 bps YoY margin improvement per year over the next couple of years.
- **Advertisement/brand spend FY27: 6–7% of revenue** (Q4 FY26 was ~4%).
- **Premiumization/distribution:** continued focus on mid-premium & premium; secondary-sales push; new sales leadership in place.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — explicit)

outlook.body:
- "Steady" Q4 performance amid competitive environment and evolving consumer demand. Revenue growth driven by **healthy volume expansion across segments**; industry pricing remains competitive.
- Volume growth +9% in Q4 reflects "improved market traction" and "strengthening consumer demand."
- Industry described as a **"total buyer's market"** — discounts dictated by market behaviour.
- Long-term concern raised by an investor: last 5–10yr sales CAGR ~2% and profitability ~2–3% — mgmt acknowledged the industry is "very competitive."
outlook.title: Demand / pipeline

outlook.body:
- **Premiumization via athleisure** is the clearest lever (mix shift lifting GM toward ~28%).
- **Sales/distribution rebuild (all done within last quarter, Q4):** appointed an all-India sales head, a separate strategy head, a dedicated **EBO head**, a separate **e-commerce head**, and **four zonal heads** — full team now in place; impact expected "in coming months."
- **Secondary-sales pivot:** shifting emphasis from primary (distributor) to secondary (distributor→retailer) movement; building a strong retail team; maintaining optimum channel inventory.
- **Exports:** flagged as a focus area for FY27 growth (currently ~3% of revenue).
- **Digital/online ad shift:** brand spend pivoting toward digital and online marketplaces.
outlook.title: Growth / optionality (premiumization, EBO/online, women's)

outlook.body:
- Consolidate the export presence in the Middle East while strategically expanding the footprint across African markets; export traction during the year came particularly from the Middle East, South Korea and Italy, contributing approximately 3% of overall revenue.
- Continue investing in manufacturing capabilities, technology, product innovation, brand development, digital initiatives and channel expansion while maintaining operational excellence and financial discipline.
- Sustain brand-building through advertising and promotional investment as a core lever for market position.
- Drive operational efficiency, prudent cost management and a strategically diversified product portfolio as the basis of performance in a competitive environment.
- Grow the Modern Trade and e-commerce channels, which contributed 5.1% of revenue during the year.
- Continue investments in automation and the SAP ERP platform to enable system-driven accounting and financial reporting, reduce manual intervention and strengthen process controls.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report carries no dedicated capex chapter and no rupee capital-expenditure quantum. Expansion is described qualitatively: the Company says it is expanding its international footprint across key export markets while deepening market penetration across India through its extensive distribution and retail network, and that going forward it intends to consolidate its presence in the Middle East while strategically expanding its footprint across African markets. Domestically, the focus is on strengthening presence in the Mid-Premium and Premium categories, scaling high-growth segments such as Athleisure, expanding distribution reach and driving efficiency-led improvements across operations. On the manufacturing side, the only named overseas expansion vehicle is Rupa Bangladesh Private Limited, a wholly-owned subsidiary incorporated in Dhaka, Bangladesh, with the principal object of undertaking manufacturing activities in Bangladesh; during the year under review it did not generate any revenue from operations. Looking ahead, the Company states it remains committed to continued investments in manufacturing capabilities, technology, product innovation, brand development, digital initiatives and channel expansion. On systems, continued investments in automation around its SAP ERP platform have enabled system-driven accounting and financial reporting. No commissioning dates, capacity additions, plant locations or project costs are disclosed. BRSR Principle 2 reports R&D and capex investments in specific technologies to improve environmental and social impacts as 0 for both FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's textile and apparel industry is a cornerstone of the economy, contributing approximately 2% to India's GDP and 11% of manufacturing GVA, with the share in GDP expected to more than double to close to 5% by 2030.
- The domestic textile and apparel market was valued at US$225 billion in 2025, growing at a CAGR of 10-12% and projected to reach US$350 billion by 2030, driven by rising domestic consumption, growing fashion and e-commerce penetration and strong export demand.
- The Indian innerwear market, valued at approximately US$10.9 billion in 2025, is projected to reach US$19.8 billion by 2034 (CAGR 6.49% during 2026-2034), supported by rising disposable incomes, urbanisation, fashion consciousness, e-commerce and organised retail penetration, and a shift towards branded and premium products.
- The Indian men's premium innerwear market was valued at US$815.8 million in 2025 and is projected to reach US$1,401.9 million by 2034 (CAGR 6.01%), supported by urbanisation, brand awareness, e-commerce and influencer-led marketing.
- The Indian lingerie market was US$5.9 billion in 2025, projected to reach US$12.0 billion by 2034 (CAGR 8.30%), with the premium lingerie segment growing faster at a 9.50% CAGR — evidence of premiumisation in women's innerwear.
- India's athleisure market, valued at US$13,880 million in 2025 and projected to reach US$22,367 million by 2034 (CAGR 5.3%), is being driven by health and wellness awareness and demand for comfortable, versatile, performance-oriented apparel, with e-commerce and quick-commerce widening reach into Tier II and Tier III cities.
- Sales volume grew 4% during FY 2025-26, led by strong demand across the economy and athleisure segments.
- The Indian kids' apparel market was US$22.57 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach US$27.17 billion by 2034 (CAGR 2.08%), driven by India's large child population, rising disposable incomes and a growing middle class.
- Domestic macro backdrop: India registered real GDP growth of 7.7% in FY 2025-26; the RBI held the repo rate at 5.25% at its April 2026 meeting and projected real GDP growth of 6.9% and CPI inflation of 4.6% for FY 2026-27, with private consumption supported by rising real incomes and cumulative rate cuts of 125 basis points during FY 2025-26.
- Headwinds flagged: conflict in West Asia since early 2026 raising energy costs and causing supply chain disruption; geopolitical tensions, evolving trade policies, raw material price volatility and supply-chain disruption remain key challenges for apparel industry participants.
- Government support — PLI Scheme for textiles, PM MITRA parks and Make in India — is strengthening manufacturing capacity and industry growth.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Rupa delivered a steady, volume-led Q4 (9% volume growth, +6.3% revenue YoY) with a sharp margin rebound (EBITDA +19.8% YoY to 12.5%) driven by athleisure mix, but the FY26 full year was a de-growth year (revenue +1.6%, EBITDA −11.6%, PAT −12.9%) reflecting an intensely competitive, buyer's-market hosiery industry; the story now hinges on a freshly rebuilt sales/distribution team, a secondary-sales pivot, and premiumization (athleisure) to deliver guided 10–12% FY27 revenue growth.
